pages.title: Start here
pages.summary: A ready crew and a short teaching job for learning core Scum and Villainy.
pages.body_markdown:
# Scum and Villainy: Quiet Orbit

A patched freighter, a breathing cargo case, and one customs checkpoint between you and a payday. This standalone starter is for 3-5 players and a GM, with six pregens to choose from and a completed Stardancer ship. Pick characters and confirm boundaries in ten minutes; no ship or character creation is required.

## Pick up and play

- [Choose a pregen](/sav/wiki/pregens): Drift the Pilot, Fuse the Mechanic, Silk the Speaker, Anchor the Muscle, Echo the Mystic, or Mercy the Stitch.
- [Meet the Quiet Orbit](/sav/wiki/quiet-orbit): your ship, modules, debts, faction relationships, and shared history are ready.
- Read [A Breathing Cargo](/sav/wiki/a-breathing-cargo) for the player briefing. Consult [the core procedure](/sav/wiki/first-job-reference) as each rule becomes relevant.
- Agree on boundaries for captivity, bodily transformation, coercion, and violence, plus a simple way to pause a scene. The job can use a strange animal instead of an intelligent captive if the table prefers.
- Introduce one crew tie and get to the handoff. Names, pronouns, and appearance can change freely.

This learning run uses **core Scum and Villainy**. Keep its Gambits, per-system Heat, ship upkeep, healing, and character abilities.

The [route atlas](/sav/atlas/) is a player-safe schematic of this job's local route, not a replacement for the published Procyon map. [Local people and factions](/sav/wiki/people-and-factions) introduce the starting cast.

This is a separate campaign entry from Ghosts of the Wayline. No existing Wayline continuity, characters, or rules choices are assumed or replaced.

pages.title: A Breathing Cargo
pages.summary: Move a living specimen through a local Rin customs checkpoint.
pages.body_markdown:
# A Breathing Cargo

**Player briefing | 2-3 hour teaching session | Rin system**

Citani, your trusted information broker, introduces **Dr. Sen Ardan**, a civilian researcher. Sen needs a sealed habitat case collected from **Kestrel Transfer**, a small bonded freight platform near Warren, and delivered to **Lantern Clinic**, an independent medical ship already waiting outside the platform's inspection perimeter.

Sen is explicit: the case contains a **living specimen**. It needs stable power, gentle handling, and no direct connection to the ship's comms. The contents belong to a disputed research consignment, so a customs team is reviewing its export permit. You have a pickup authorization and the habitat manual, not an exemption from inspection.

**Pay:** 6 CRED for delivering the intact case and its live occupant to the clinic. If you cannot make the handoff, Sen offers 3 CRED for returning the living specimen safely to their care. This fallback is agreed before departure. Your crew pays 1 CRED ship upkeep afterward, from its funds; that is not a hidden reduction in Sen's price.

**The route:** collect from the transfer platform, cross a local customs inspection corridor, and reach the clinic. All three are in Rin; no jumpgate or inter-system trip is required. You already have a ship that can make the journey.

**The case:** about the size of a large instrument trunk. Two handles; 2 personal load if carried by one person, or 1 each if carried together. In the cargo hold it takes cargo space, not anyone's personal load. Carrying it is not a separate roll unless the situation makes it risky. It is already powered for the planned journey.

**Known approaches:** use the public freight desk with the authorization, negotiate with the bonded-cargo clerk, or enter through a maintenance access with suitable preparation. A transport plan needs a route and means; other plans are welcome. Choose load, answer a couple of useful questions, roll engagement, and begin at the first obstacle.

The station staff are doing a job, not waiting to die for a container. How quietly do you want to handle this?

*The job, station, clinic, and research dispute are original campaign material. Citani is a published Stardancer contact. Art and portrait credits are linked in the site footer.*

pages.title: The Quiet Orbit
pages.summary: A completed Stardancer with starting systems, upgrades, CRED, and faction ties.
pages.body_markdown:
# The Quiet Orbit

**Completed Stardancer crew | Professional reputation | CF-350 Scarab-class freighter**

You are partners already. Last month you delivered replacement air scrubbers to a habitat that could not afford a Guild contract. Citani has offered the crew another introduction. Nobody has to recruit the others during this session.

## Ship record

| Field | Starting value |
|---|---|
| Crew quality | 0 |
| Engines | 2/4; Jump Drive installed; one unused module slot |
| Hull | 2/4; Cargo Hold and Smuggling Compartments installed |
| Comms | 1/3; Fake Transponder installed |
| Weapons | 0/2; no ship weapons installed |
| Auxiliary modules | Galley, Medical Bay |
| Training | Insight |
| Special ability | The Getaway |
| Ship CRED | 2/4 |
| Debt and skipped upkeep | 0 each |
| Damage and shields | No damage; no Shields upgrade |
| Crew XP | Empty tracker on the supplied Stardancer sheet |
| Starting Gambits | 2 at the start of each job |
| Heat / Wanted | Rin 0/0; Holt 0/0; Iota 0/0; Brekk 0/0 |

**Upkeep is 1 CRED:** floor((Engines 2 + Hull 2 + Comms 1 + Weapons 0 + crew quality 0) / 4) = 1. Use the arithmetic for this actual ship, not a generic suggested starting upkeep. A full 6-CRED payoff plus the existing 2 leaves 7 after upkeep; distribute or spend at least 3 before the next job because the ship normally holds only 4 CRED.

## What the ship can do

**The Getaway:** the whole crew has potency when using Scramble or Helm to escape capture or run a blockade. Delivery jobs get +1d on engagement. It does not give a die on every Helm roll. Core p. 124.

**Fake Transponder:** offers a false ship identity; it does not magically fix every inconsistent cargo manifest. **Smuggling Compartments:** provide concealed cargo storage; a sufficiently focused search can still find it. **Medical Bay:** +1d to crew recovery rolls. **Insight Training:** a training activity on that attribute marks 2 XP instead of 1. No workshop, AI module, armed escort, or free cohort is included.

## Creation accounting

The base Stardancer has Engines 1, Hull 2, Comms 0, Weapons 0 and crew quality 0, plus Jump Drive, Cargo Hold, Smuggling Compartments, Galley, and Insight Training. We selected Engines +1 and Comms +1 for the two system improvements. The two additional upgrades are Fake Transponder and Medical Bay; the Comms rating provides the transponder's module slot.

You kept the initial 2 CRED by owing the faction that helped with the systems a favor, rather than paying them. No CRED was spent on extra status changes, and no crew-quality increase was purchased.

| Faction | Status | Creation choice in this campaign |
|---|---:|---|
| Cobalt Syndicate | +1 | Helped with system improvements; you owe a favor |
| Mendicants | +1 | Helped source the Medical Bay |
| Counters Guild | -2 | Lost disputed medical equipment in the upgrade deal; no mollifying payment |
| Conclave 01 | +1 | Friendly with Citani in this campaign |
| Church of Stellar Flame | -1 | Hostile to Citani in this campaign |
| All others | 0 | Until play establishes a relationship |

**Favorite contact:** Citani, a reclusive information broker. The particular contact relationships above are original campaign choices, not canonical claims about Citani. No faction is at war with you. The Cobalt favor is an obligation, not numeric debt; no invented ward-boss tithe applies.

## Crew XP

Review the four core triggers at session end: a successful transport/smuggling job; contending with challenges above your station; strengthening or changing your reputation; expressing the crew's goals, drives, internal conflict, or essential nature. Mark 1 XP for each that occurred, or 2 if it occurred repeatedly. Core pp. 51 and 122-125.

Crew quality, ship system quality, a faction's Tier, and a reputation label are different things. This campaign has no Blades-style crew Tier/hold/turf ladder or spendable Rep resource.

pages.title: Choose a pregen
pages.summary: Six complete scoundrels for a ten-minute pickup.
pages.body_markdown:
# Choose your crew

Six complete scoundrels; choose three to five. Take a role that sounds enjoyable rather than trying to cover every rule. Unchosen characters are away on personal business and contribute no extra turns, downtime activities, or abilities.

| Pregen | Role | Pick for |
|---|---|---|
| [Drift](/sav/wiki/pregen-drift) | Pilot | Daring approaches and escapes |
| [Fuse](/sav/wiki/pregen-fuse) | Mechanic | Hacking, engineering, and ship repairs |
| [Silk](/sav/wiki/pregen-silk) | Speaker | Negotiations, access, and catching lies |
| [Anchor](/sav/wiki/pregen-anchor) | Muscle | Protecting people and applying force |
| [Echo](/sav/wiki/pregen-echo) | Mystic | Way phenomena and strange encounters |
| [Mercy](/sav/wiki/pregen-mercy) | Stitch | Science, care, and recovery |

For three players, Drift/Fuse/Silk is a useful mix. No playbook is mandatory: another character can Helm, and the job has practical responses to the cargo's behavior without a Mystic or Stitch.

Every pregen has seven action dots, preserving the playbook's initial three and adding four with a maximum of 2 per action. Each also has the S&V **unique starting ability plus one chosen special ability**, resistance/vice ratings, gear, connections, and empty trackers. Keep the supplied Player Sheets open for marking boxes, or record changes on the pregen page. The Blank Muscle sheet is optional for someone building a custom character later; it is not a different playbook.

## Ten-minute pickup

Choose characters (3 minutes), read the [ship record](/sav/wiki/quiet-orbit) (2), agree boundaries and a pause signal (3), then introduce one crew tie each (2). Go straight to [the briefing](/sav/wiki/a-breathing-cargo). Save mechanical rebuilding and a full session zero for later.

pages.title: Your first S&V job
pages.summary: Core actions, Gambits, equipment, and the complete aftermath loop.
pages.body_markdown:
# Your first S&V job

**Active rules: core Scum and Villainy.** Printed core page numbers are ten less than the page number in the supplied full-text PDF.

## Action and consequence

Describe your goal and approach; choose the action. The GM explains position and effect before the roll. Roll d6s equal to the action rating, keep the highest. At zero dice, roll two and keep the lower; that cannot produce a critical. A 6 succeeds, a 4/5 succeeds with a consequence, and a 1-3 goes badly according to position. Multiple 6s give a critical when rolling a positive pool.

Before rolling, push for 2 stress for +1d or improved effect, or take an agreed Devil's Bargain for +1d. The push bonus die and bargain cannot stack. One ally may assist for 1 stress and +1d. The crew may spend one Gambit for another +1d. Fictional positioning, gear, setups, and special abilities also matter.

After hearing a consequence, resistance automatically reduces or avoids it as the GM determines. Roll the relevant attribute; stress cost is 6 minus the highest result, while a critical clears 1 stress. Attributes count the actions with a dot in their column, not all the dots. A resistance-only bonus does not increase vice dice. Suitable armor can also absorb a consequence when the fiction permits; mark the relevant box and item load.

## Gambits are shared

Reset the crew pool to **2** at the start of a job for this Stardancer. Any PC may spend one for +1d on an action. A risky action with a 6 or critical normally generates one Gambit if you did not spend one on that roll. Controlled or desperate rolls do not normally generate one. One qualifying roll grants one Gambit, not one per 6. Specific abilities can change these conditions.

Echo's Mystic starting ability can spend a Gambit instead of a stress cost, including a push or resistance. That is a separate permission from buying a bonus die; account for what was actually purchased. Never assume the crew has infinite Gambits. Core p. 121 and the Mystic rules apply.

## Flashbacks and teamwork

A flashback establishes earlier preparation for a stated stress cost and a roll if uncertain. It cannot erase a fact already established. A flashback to a downtime activity costs 1 CRED as normal. Assist, setup, protect, and group actions are available. A group-action leader takes 1 stress per participant who rolls 1-3; the group uses the best result. Nobody must make a group roll for a clear, safe exit.

## Equipment and space

Choose light 3 or normal 5 load; the supplied sheet offers heavy 6, within the core book's heavy 6-8 range. For this starter, use 6 if choosing heavy. Reveal items as needed rather than packing everything in advance. Refreshing load on the ship does not erase stress or harm; use the core gear procedure when there is time and access.

| Standard item | Load |
|---|---:|
| Blaster pistol; second pistol; melee weapon | 1 each |
| Heavy blaster | 2 |
| Detonator | 1 |
| Hacking tools; repair tools; spy gear | 1 each |
| Medkit; armor; spacesuit | 2 each |
| Communicator; illicit drugs | 0 |

Fine gear improves relevant quality; it is not automatically +1d. A spacesuit permits EVA, but still needs its load and air supply. Ship storage is not free personal equipment while away from the ship. A case does not become a crew upgrade because you carried it once.

## After the job

Receive payoff, pay or skip upkeep, assess **Rin's** Heat, apply known faction changes, roll an entanglement from the wanted-level column for the system where the ship ends the job, then take downtime. At Wanted 0 this is a single d6 on the Wanted 0 table, not the Blades wanted-level dice pool. Heat reaches a new Wanted level at **8**, with overflow retained. Do not copy the Blades nine-Heat threshold.

Each PC normally has two downtime activities, one at war. Extra activities cost 1 CRED; there is no Rep payment option. Silk also has a restricted extra activity for acquire asset or lay low. Fuse has an extra free repair activity from their selected ability. Activities need fictional access. Laying low requires being in another system; a quick orbit around Warren is not enough.

Recovery clears level 1 harm after treatment; if harm remains, advance the **six-segment** healing clock. Filling it clears **all** harm; taking more harm before completion resets that clock. The Medical Bay adds +1d to recovery rolls. Ordinary repair costs 1 CRED and an activity per ship damage; Fuse's ability changes their repair cost and allowance. Core pp. 176-193.

Stress, harm, ship damage, debt, and per-system Heat persist. Review personal and crew XP triggers; do not reward only successful rolls. Desperate actions mark attribute XP when rolled. No pregen needs to invent trauma to earn XP.

pages.title: People and factions
pages.summary: The known cast and starting relationships around the ship.
pages.body_markdown:
# People around the Quiet Orbit

These are the people and relationships the crew knows before the first job. Job-specific people and placements are original additions to the published Procyon sector.

## People

**Citani — reclusive information broker.** Your favorite Stardancer contact. Introduced Sen and vouches that the fee exists. Values discretion and reliable introductions, not obedience.

**Dr. Sen Ardan — civilian researcher.** Needs a living research specimen moved to medical care. Has pickup authority, a habitat manual, and an export dispute. Offers 6 CRED for live delivery or 3 for safe return if delivery proves impossible.

**Mira Dax — bonded-cargo clerk.** Can release the consignment. Wants a signed record she can defend to her supervisor. Treating her as a person is useful.

**Inspector Hale — local customs officer.** Can inspect outbound manifests and hold departure clearance. Has a team and a job to do. An authorization to collect cargo does not automatically clear export.

**Asha Venn — tug captain.** Runs a working tug between nearby platforms. Knows service lanes and values reciprocal favors. An ally is someone you negotiate with, not a free crew upgrade.

**Dr. Olan Vey — Lantern Clinic physician.** Works aboard an independent medical ship outside the inspection perimeter. Can provide legitimate care and receive the consignment. The clinic's neutrality is a practice it negotiates, not immunity from every faction.

## Starting factions

See the [ship record](/sav/wiki/quiet-orbit) for exact status and creation accounting. Published faction identities are summarized here; these particular relationships are campaign choices.

- **Cobalt Syndicate (+1):** labor organization and criminal enterprise. Helped improve the ship's systems; the crew owes a favor.
- **Mendicants (+1):** itinerant healers. Helped source the Medical Bay; the clinic is independent unless play establishes a connection.
- **Counters Guild (−2):** controls finance. Lost a disputed medical equipment deal when the ship acquired upgrades.
- **Conclave 01 (+1):** independent Urbots seeking liberation. Friendly through Citani in this campaign.
- **Church of Stellar Flame (−1):** an established religious power opposed to the crew's contact here.

Local customs is not a new sector-wide faction, and no starting faction is at war with the crew. Select a known site in the [route atlas](/sav/atlas/) for public access and jurisdiction notes. Faction presence does not imply exclusive ownership.

pages.title: Atlas notes
pages.summary: Original local route diagram; all starter sites are in Rin.
pages.body_markdown:
# Local route atlas

[Open the atlas](/sav/atlas/). It is an interactive schematic for **A Breathing Cargo**, not a canonical map of the Rin system. Kestrel Transfer and Lantern Clinic are original locations near Warren. The inspection corridor is a local traffic-control route, not an inter-system gate. All job nodes are in Rin; traveling between them does not qualify as laying low in another system.

Choose a site in the diagram or the keyboard-accessible directory. Filter by the crew, station operations, customs, independent medical care, or local context. These labels describe access and jurisdiction at the start of the job, not exclusive faction territory. The map contains only facts the crew can know from its briefing; private cargo behavior and later plot leads stay in staff-only pages.

- **Warren:** published Rin location; context for this small freight route, not a claim to map every port.
- **Kestrel bonded desk:** pickup authorization and release records; Mira is the useful first contact.
- **Quiet Orbit berth:** the crew's ship, load access, and departure point.
- **Inspection corridor:** manifest inspection and outbound clearance; a medical escort can be negotiated.
- **Lantern Clinic:** independent receiving medical ship beyond the inspection perimeter, still inside Rin.

Lines show a known route, not the only legal player choice. Negotiate a tow, take another service lane, or return safely to Sen if the situation calls for it. Map placement does not establish a hidden obstacle. The [people page](/sav/wiki/people-and-factions) and [ship record](/sav/wiki/quiet-orbit) list actual starting faction statuses.

The diagram can grow after play: add locations and public faction influence when the crew learns them. Do not embed unrevealed GM clocks or secrets in a supposedly player-safe static JSON file.

# Sources and artwork

This is an unofficial personal campaign for **Scum and Villainy**, by Stras Acimovic and John LeBoeuf-Little, published by Evil Hat Productions. Their games, setting, and artwork belong to their respective rights holders. The supplied purchased/reference PDFs stay in the local Docs folder; the site does not distribute the rulebooks, character-sheet PDFs, or full rules text.

## Rules consulted

- SaV-Release-6x9-Full_Text.pdf: the core book. Printed page p is PDF page p + 10.
- SaV-Release-Sheets.pdf: combined play and GM sheets; used to check load, action starts, and ship options.
- SaV-Release-Player_Sheets.pdf: used to validate pregen playbooks and equipment boxes.
- SaV-Release-GM_Sheets.pdf: table procedure reference.
- SaV-Release-Sheets_Blank_Muscle.pdf: optional blank custom character sheet; not a separate playbook.
- SaV-Release-Blank_System.pdf: a blank system worksheet for later original locations.

The original job selects entries from S&V pp. 127, 338–339 and develops a new situation from them. Pregens use paraphrased ability descriptions, not reproduced sheets. Kestrel Transfer, Lantern Clinic, the Quiet Orbit's history, and job-specific cast are original campaign additions. Faction names and Procyon setting are published S&V material. Art is illustrative casting, not an assertion that a photographed person endorses this fiction.

## Space image

**Carina Nebula Jets (NIRCam Narrowband Filters)**. Credit: **NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI, J. DePasquale (STScI)**. [Source](https://esawebb.org/images/carinanebula3/), [ESA/Webb terms](https://esawebb.org/copyright/), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Source-provided screensize image, no retouching by this project. The real Carina Nebula is mood imagery, not a claim about Procyon's astronomy.

## Portraits

These are the sketch-treated photographs from the owner's previously supplied Blades Portraits collection, reused as a different fictional cast. Original photos use the [Unsplash License](https://unsplash.com/license); the FotoSketcher treatment was supplied by the owner and its editor is not identified in the folder metadata. They are not public-domain portraits. No new retouching was done. The downloadable asset manifest records original photo identifiers, source files, source links, treatment notes, and SHA-256 hashes.

- **Fuse** — original photograph by **Cesar Rincon**; photo ID `XHVpWcr5grQ`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18mSQgwKDAvE7yEfhuKseapaO2RbflKrW/view?usp=drivesdk).
- **Anchor** — original photograph by **Philip Martin**; photo ID `5aGUyCW_PJw`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KVB1o7w_aXY-RfBi6P2gltyOv40ZjK5B/view?usp=drivesdk).
- **Echo** — original photograph by **Vladimir Palyanov**; photo ID `m5e4RX_QwKg`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wWY_iDTd3RJsNHGQboZNft_v0u66R_De/view?usp=drivesdk).
- **Silk** — original photograph by **Ahmed Syed**; photo ID `rXRFce8WOnU`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1U0VM6isFjj1I7naiKhXN_MwLLqqAHjMg/view?usp=drivesdk).
- **Mercy** — original photograph by **Kimson Doan**; photo ID `HD8KlyWRYYM`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OwAhJu67MUN3xEYENPq4SUT53vN0v3u-/view?usp=drivesdk).
- **Drift** — original photograph by **Oliver Ragfelt**; photo ID `khV4fTy6-D8`. [Supplied sketch source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1fFmQveN4c10-hkjFinJGgiwdpLGd2NEn/view?usp=drivesdk).

[Machine-readable art manifest](/static/sav/manifest.json).

## Route atlas

The SVG route diagram is original code-native campaign artwork. It shows local job relationships and approximate schematic positions, not canonical orbital distances, a published star chart, or an adaptation of the supplied Blank System artwork. It contains no copied map art or rulebook pages. [Atlas notes](/sav/wiki/atlas-notes) explain known sites and faction labels.

pages.title: GM: A Breathing Cargo
pages.summary: Private teaching-job preparation, clocks, stakes, and aftermath.
pages.body_markdown:
# GM: A Breathing Cargo

**Core S&V only • 3–5 PCs • 2–3 hours • private preparation.** Read the player brief and ship record first. This job teaches a complete loop, including payoff and downtime. It is a situation with several exits, not a required sequence of rolls.

## The job-table recipe

These are deliberately selected results, not a claim that dice were rolled: the Stardancer's lucrative opportunity **living cargo, difficult to contain** (core p. 127); civilian client **academic/scholar** and underworld work **smuggle/courier** (p. 338); complications **watched by Hegemonic forces** and **strong Precursor/Way presence** (p. 339). Kestrel Transfer, Lantern Clinic, and all job-specific SPCs are original additions to Rin. Citani and Warren are published setting elements.

## What is really in the case

**Morrow** is a living, bioelectric organism recovered from an abandoned research habitat. It senses patterns in the Way and repeats familiar signals through nearby maintenance circuits. It is intelligent enough to express preferences, frightened, and trying to find quiet. Its habitat has a paper trail that multiple offices claim authority over. Sen knows it is alive and unusual; Sen has not recognized its intelligence. There is no secret plan to sell it after the crew does the right thing.

An automated customs interrogation broadcast agitates Morrow. It starts reproducing that pattern in nearby nonessential systems; connected equipment may open an access panel or wake an escape pod. The case is not a magical remote hack of any ship at any distance. Physical isolation, a filtered power supply, medical stabilization, changing the broadcast pattern, or communication can all help. No Mystic is required. If the table chose an animal version, use learned responses instead of words, with the same practical solutions.

If Silk uses Player, give an honest assessment: Sen intends medical care and payment; Sen is withholding no known sale or ambush. The paperwork dispute is real. Do not invalidate a lie-reading ability to preserve a twist.

## Pacing

| Minutes | Aim |
|---|---|
| 0–10 | Choose pregens, crew tie, boundaries |
| 10–20 | Brief, load, one useful information question, plan and engagement |
| 20–45 | Collect the case; teach one action and consequence |
| 45–80 | Inspection or a route around it; reveal cargo behavior |
| 80–100 | Delivery, withdrawal, or another chosen resolution |
| 100–135 | Payoff, upkeep, Heat, entanglement, two activities, XP |
| 135–150 | Debrief and choose a next lead |

For a strict two hours, end the job by minute 80 and reserve at least 30 minutes for aftermath. Cut an obstacle, never the whole downtime lesson. Five players should get one meaningful decision each, not five compulsory rolls at every station.

## Opening at the obstacle

Read: *The bonded desk light turns amber as your pickup code scans. Beyond the glass, a trunk-sized habitat case breathes cool vapor. A public address asks all outbound traffic to keep comms open for inspection. The clerk looks from the code to your ship registration: “Medical transfer? I can release it. Your exit clearance is another department.”*

Confirm the agreed **6 CRED** live delivery, **3 CRED** safe return to Sen, and known **1 CRED upkeep**. A transport plan needs a route and means. Use the normal engagement pool: start at 1d, apply the core fictional factors, and add The Getaway's +1d if this is a delivery plan. A straightforward neutral transport can therefore start at 2d; adjust from the actual plan, not an invented mandatory penalty. On a 6 begin controlled, 4/5 risky, 1–3 desperate; critical begins beyond the opening obstacle. Do not roll engagement again for every scene.

At controlled entry, Mira has cleared the pickup and asks a routine question. Risky: clearance is paused while she asks why the destination changed to a ship. Desperate: a customs inspection team is already at the pallet; begin with their imminent seizure stated openly. These are starting situations, not extra harm or Heat automatically inflicted by engagement.

## Three pressures, several answers

**The handoff.** Clerk Mira needs a defensible release record. Sway can frame the legitimate medical urgency; Consort can use a relevant relationship; Hack can redirect the clearance queue; Skulk can use maintenance access. If the code and explanation plainly suffice, release the cargo without rolling. A risky partial success might get release but alert inspector Hale (Inspection lock +1), or require a documented guarantor. Failure may leave the case behind the desk with a new demand; never delete every possible approach.

**The corridor.** Hale wants a complete manifest, not a shootout. Official transfer, a changed registry through the Fake Transponder, a tow arrangement with Asha, disabling the local broadcast, a quiet maintenance departure, and a blockade run are all possible. Typical station security is quality I; it is not automatically the full Tier of every Guild in the sector. Describe any actual superior equipment before it constrains effect. Scramble/Helm escapes receive The Getaway potency. Drift's Ace Pilot and the crew ability may reinforce the same fictional advantage; do not mechanically multiply identical potency into automatic extreme effect.

**The cargo.** As the interrogation broadcast begins, the habitat taps a slow pattern against its frame. A display draws a route toward the clinic. Offer that information before asking how PCs investigate. Study/Doctor can establish a meaningful response; Rig can isolate supply; Hack can redirect the interrogation system; Attune can reach a mind through the Way. Normal human kindness plus clear gestures can work without a roll when nothing contests it. The complication becomes hazardous only if pressure is active and the response uncertain. The party can simply take the powered case to safe care.

## Only two clocks

Show **Inspection lock 0/4** and **Habitat distress 0/4**. They measure fictional developments, not elapsed table minutes. Announce the clock and number of ticks as a consequence before resistance; use 1/2/3 ticks for minor/moderate/severe consequences when appropriate. No automatic tick for every roll, every six, or every real-time interval.

- Inspection lock full: the regular departure lane closes and Hale orders the ship held. Alternatives remain: negotiate medical release, accept an escort, use the maintenance lane with a new danger, or run the blockade. It does not retroactively confiscate the case or disable the ship.
- Habitat distress full: Morrow opens its outer service housing and reaches for the nearest powered refuge. This exposes the creature and changes the transport problem; it does not kill it. Offer portable life support, containment repair, moving together into the ship's medical bay, or the escape pod as a revised route.

Use an immediate consequence instead of a clock tick where that is clearer: level 1 “arc burn,” a dropped tool, lost authorization, or worsening position. Avoid charging harm, Heat, a clock, and lost effect for one mild consequence. Choose a consequence, then let resistance or armor do its work.

## Teach through one example

Fuse bypasses a service latch with Hack 2. GM: risky/standard; a 4/5 opens it and advances Inspection lock by 2. Fuse pushes (+1d, 2 stress), Silk assists (+1d, 1 stress), and the crew spends a Gambit (+1d): 5d, highest kept. On a 5, the latch opens and the warning activates. Fuse can resist the warning with Insight 3d (Hack, Rig, Study have dots). A highest 5 costs 1 stress; the GM says whether the warning is reduced to one tick or prevented by the established fiction. Because a Gambit was spent, even a 6 would not replenish one from this roll.

Offer a flashback when a player says “I wish we'd prepared a medical export declaration.” Quote a stress cost before the flashback. A perfectly plausible existing blank form might be 0; arranging a compliant official under pressure might be 1–2 and require a roll. It cannot undo the fact Hale has already read the manifest. Prompt a setup or assist if someone wants to help; do not force each PC into the same action.

## Endings and payment

The clinic will accept a living intelligent occupant as a patient, not inventory. Dr. Olan asks for the case history and the crew's consent to describe what happened. Respect the crew's boundaries about research and custody. Sen pays 6 for a living delivery in the case; if the crew makes a medically necessary alternate safe transfer, Sen honors the same fee. If they choose the advertised safe return, pay 3. Walking away without delivery or safe return yields no job payment, but do not remove other earned resources. A dead occupant means the agreed success condition was not met; discuss how the fiction reached that outcome, never invent a lethal “clock full” surprise.

Negotiating freedom, a future visit, or a different caretaker is possible. Do not require a moral speech or the “correct” ending. Escorted delivery, paperwork-heavy delivery, a chaotic escape, and quiet success are all valid sessions.

## Run the aftermath on screen

1. **Payoff:** normally 6 CRED. No Blades Rep award. Existing ship funds 2 + fee 6 − upkeep 1 = 7; distribute/spend at least 3 to respect ship capacity 4. Each PC also has personal capacity 4. Record actual shares.
2. **Upkeep:** pay 1 from ship funds; if skipped, use core skipped-upkeep/debt rules rather than inventing an extra tithe. Fuse's repair ability does not waive upkeep.
3. **Heat in Rin:** choose the core band from what happened: 0 contained/quiet, 1 smooth, 2 normal, 4 loud, 6 devastating; apply relevant core modifiers, including high profile/artifacts +1, Hegemonic citizen killing or mass destruction/illegal weapons +2, gate/hyperlane damage +3. A quiet permit fix is not automatically a loud job. At 8 advance Wanted, clear eight, retain overflow. Other systems stay unchanged.
4. **Factions:** explain any change earned by a consequential choice. Clinic access is not automatically Mendicant membership. Honoring the Cobalt favor can happen later; don't charge it again at payoff.
5. **Entanglement:** in Rin, roll one d6 in its current Wanted column (normally 0); 6 escalates to the next table as the book directs. Use the actual result, reskinned to known people. Allow the crew to address it through play. Do not replace the roll with a mandatory chase.
6. **Downtime:** each active PC gets two activities because the crew is not at war; extras cost 1 CRED. Use real stress/harm from play; demonstrate recovery only if someone is hurt. Medical Bay +1d and Mercy's applicable Physicker bonus can stack. Fuse has the extra repair activity and free repair supplied by Bailing Wire. Silk's extra activity is acquire asset/lay low only; lay low requires another system. A safe local return to the clinic does not meet that requirement.
7. **XP:** read character and crew triggers aloud. Training normally grants XP; core recovery is a six-clock clearing all harm.

Read [the supporting cast](/sav/wiki/gm-supporting-cast) for reactions and [After the quiet orbit](/sav/wiki/gm-next-arc) for opportunities driven by the outcome.

pages.title: GM supporting cast

pages.body_markdown:
# GM supporting cast

Private cards. SPCs act through the fiction and the PCs' action/fortune rolls; they do not need PC stat blocks or their own combat turns. Quality is a starting comparison, not an automatic effect penalty. Ordinary dock security is quality I. Introduce stronger equipment openly before it matters.

## Citani — the introduction

Published Stardancer contact; this portrayal is original. **Wants:** introductions that leave everyone alive and still answering calls. **Knows:** Sen is solvent, the permit is disputed, the clinic is real; not Morrow's nature. **Leverage:** information, a discreet introduction to Asha. **Limit:** no power to erase customs records. **Reaction:** rewards candor with the next lead, grows wary of making civilians expendable. Voice: concise, careful questions. “What did they actually ask you to carry?”

## Dr. Sen Ardan — the client

**Wants:** the specimen alive under proper medical care. **Knows:** it reacts to electromagnetic and Way activity; no direct comms connection; has not identified sentience. **Leverage:** 6 CRED, pickup code, manual, fallback return arrangement. **Capability:** Study/medical expertise quality I; no fighting force. **Pressure:** professional reputation, competing claims on the consignment. **Reaction:** believes credible evidence of intelligence, agrees to patient treatment and the promised fee. Anger at a needless death, not an automatic betrayal. Player detects no hidden sale. “I can tell you the power tolerance. I can't tell you what it's dreaming.”

## Mira Dax — the desk

**Wants:** a clean handoff and an uneventful shift. **Knows:** clearance queue, service access, who can authorize exceptions. **Leverage:** release timestamp and a call to Hale. **Limit:** cannot authorize export herself. **Reaction:** a credible guarantor or signed medical urgency gets consideration; intimidation may gain compliance with a recorded alarm. Won't fight to the death over a desk. “Whose name goes in this field?”

## Inspector Hale — the border

**Wants:** a documented resolution without embarrassing the office. **Knows:** an irregular research consignment is leaving; not the occupant's intelligence. **Leverage:** inspection hold, two officers, scanner, lane control. **Capability:** quality I, sidearms and armor only if revealed; no cruiser or supernatural detection. **Reaction:** an honestly negotiated escort can succeed; false records invite scrutiny when inconsistencies appear. Pursues an actual dangerous departure, but accepts a clear concession. “Show me where this transfer ends.”

## Asha Venn — another route

**Wants:** working pilots to help one another; fuel and a reciprocal tow favor. **Knows:** local tug routes and the clinic's position. **Leverage:** legitimate tug schedule, mechanical couplers. **Capability:** a small civilian tug, quality I; not an armed ship. **Reaction:** accepts a reasonable favor, declines being a human shield without warning, may set up the crew's route. Her cooperation does not require adding a permanent cohort. “You need a tow, or you need someone to look like they're towing you?”

## Dr. Olan Vey — the destination

**Wants:** patients stabilized and the clinic still able to operate tomorrow. **Knows:** containment medicine, not a complete theory of the Way. **Leverage:** medical receiving record and safe habitat. **Capability:** treatment quality I; the crew's own Med Bay is separate. **Reaction:** offers a practical alternative if the case opens; refuses invasive experiments without consent. Doesn't demand the crew join a faction. “A history first. Who has been deciding what it needs?”

## Morrow — not inventory

**Wants:** quiet, safe power, and choices about where it goes. **Knows:** recurring signals, a remembered habitat, a broken fragment of navigation data. **Capability:** bioelectric signaling through adjacent connected maintenance systems; no arbitrary remote possession. **Pressure:** repeated interrogation pulses. **Reaction:** copies patterns when scared; cooperates with repeated gentle signals. Full distress clock opens the service housing, not lethal harm. It can communicate a preference through displays, gestures, or Attune; the crew need not roll a Mystic to grant it care. If using an animal, replace intent and navigation testimony with trained recognition of a signal.

## Rook Hessa — optional next-session courier

**Wants:** a paying route contract before the Guild captures it. **Knows:** someone is bidding on an incomplete navigation archive. **Leverage:** another ship and one access code. **Reaction:** a rival who can become a partner; no compulsory betrayal. Keep Rook out of the teaching job unless there is spare time. Introduce at debrief as one possible next lead, not a surprise fourth obstacle.

pages.title: GM: After the quiet orbit
pages.summary: Three optional jobs with competing faction offers and consequences.
pages.body_markdown:
# GM: After the quiet orbit

**Optional follow-on opportunities for the core S&V learning run.** Nothing here is required to explain the teaching job. Start from what the crew did and whom they now care about. These notes are private; let public discoveries enter the wiki through play.

## The larger question

Who can claim ownership of a route, an Urbot, or a living intelligence? Morrow's remembered signal may connect isolated habitats that cannot afford Guild-controlled transport. It is a lead, not a prophecy or a key that alone destroys the Hegemony. If Morrow is an animal, the same signal appears in its old tracking harness and research records; do not force intelligence back into the chosen version.

Transfer the social pressure behind Blades' new factions into **existing S&V powers**. Conclave 01 already gives created people an autonomy movement. Cobalt Syndicate supplies labor and transport pressure. The Guilds have commercial and technical interests. The Church can offer a sincere, dangerous interpretation of a Way phenomenon. Add individual advocates and disagreements rather than giving each faction one moral personality.

## Three people with incompatible offers

- **Tess-9, Conclave 01 advocate:** wants the archive copied without publishing identities of fugitives using its routes. Offers technical assistance and shelter, not free advanced ship systems. Wants Morrow treated as a participant if intelligent.
- **Overseer Ilex, Guild negotiator:** wants exclusive route surveys to prevent untested transit disasters; also expects profitable monopoly. Offers a legal charter and removal of a specific equipment claim. Can honor a negotiated deal; is not secretly behind every event.
- **Sister Vael, Church navigator:** believes the signal is evidence of a sacred boundary and wants a supervised expedition. Offers charts and a volunteer, with explicit restrictions on artifact handling. Some of the warnings may be justified.

The crew's Cobalt contact **Jori Pell** calls in the already established favor: carry a habitat workers' representative and replacement seals. That job must remain viable even if the crew declines every mystery above. Counters Guild −2 creates paperwork and creditor pressure, not instant war or an unavoidable seizure.

## Opportunity 1: Salvage with voices

A derelict relay in **Holt** has a fragment matching the signal. Client can be Tess-9 or a Guild surveyor, depending on the crew's choice. Job: salvage the navigation spool and recover any survivors. Advertise **8 CRED** plus clearly stated salvage rights. The extra travel allows an actual different-system lay-low activity later, but don't pretend local Rin travel already did so.

Obstacles: unstable rotation; a rescue beacon replaying old distress calls; a salvage claimant with a valid partial title. Discovery: an independent Urbot has kept the relay alive and wants safe passage, not theft of their memory. No need to steal a person's core to get the navigation fragment; copying, bargaining, repairs, or retrieving a backup are possible. If the crew ignores the signal, use this as an ordinary salvage contract instead.

## Opportunity 2: A witness, not cargo

The workers' representative on Jori's favor run has evidence of unsafe Guild routing. The job is safe transport and a chosen hearing destination, not compulsory revolutionary recruitment. The Cobalt obligation is paid by this delivery, not an infinite chain of favors. Offer **4 CRED expenses/pay** so “favor” is not a secret upkeep trap. Say who pays, how much, and when before engagement.

Obstacles: a competing courier offers a fast route with a catch; the witness wants to stop at an endangered habitat; a customs office requests a lawful interview. The crew decides whose promise matters. Evidence can support a public hearing, private settlement, or independent distribution. Those outcomes change faction status through named actions, not a prewritten betrayal.

## Opportunity 3: The route belongs to whom?

A buyer offers **10 CRED** to demonstrate a reconstructed local bypass at a public shipping auction. Tess-9 asks for an anonymous safe-access copy. Vael warns that one section crosses an active Way disturbance. Ilex offers paid licensing instead. Telegraph that testing the dangerous route can put lives at risk; there is a slower safe route with weaker commercial value. No unannounced mandatory gate-damage consequence.

Obstacles: secure the relay calibration; negotiate who accompanies the demonstration; choose what to publish and what to conceal. A successful job can end with an independent cooperative route, a licensed route, a hidden rescue corridor, or the crew rejecting the whole deal. The archive is a useful contested asset, not an excuse to award free crew quality or ignore module slots.

## Run clocks between jobs

Use four six-segment faction clocks, initially 0, adjusted from the actual starter outcome:

- **Guild exclusive charter:** advances when offices secure surveys and signatures. Full means a legal claim and enforcement offer; the crew can contest it.
- **Conclave safe corridor:** advances when advocates gain willing partners and secure copies. Full creates a usable safe network, not automatic sector liberation.
- **Church quarantine case:** advances when credible danger reports accumulate or Vael secures backing. Full means an attempted restriction; negotiate, defy, or investigate.
- **Habitat supply failure:** advances only after named disruptions or unattended needs, not because the GM wants urgency. Full creates a concrete shortage and rescue job, not offscreen mass death by default.

After each job, choose relevant faction actions and use the core fortune procedure where uncertain. Announce what the crew could reasonably learn. Not every clock ticks every downtime. Advance one or two pressures that actually moved. Hostility should produce offers, obstacles, and choices before an unavoidable confrontation.

## Keep learning through play

Continue with core S&V. Introduce rules as they become relevant, and use the session log to record what the crew learns and changes.
